templates.pattern: A bitmap image is [W] pixels wide and [H] pixels tall with a colour depth of [D] bits per pixel. Calculate the file size of the image in bits.
templates.explanation:
File size in bits = width × height × colour depth
= [W] × [H] × [D]
= [RESULT] bits

Every pixel requires [D] bits to store its colour information. More colours need more bits per pixel but produce larger files.

templates.pattern: A file has a size of [BITS] bits. Calculate the size of the file in bytes.
templates.explanation:
File size in bytes = bits ÷ 8
= [BITS] ÷ 8
= [RESULT] bytes

1 byte = 8 bits. This conversion is used constantly in Computer Science — always check whether you are working in bits or bytes.

templates.pattern: A file has a size of [BYTES] bytes. Calculate the size of the file in kilobytes (KB).
templates.explanation:
File size in KB = bytes ÷ 1024
= [BYTES] ÷ 1024
= [RESULT] KB

1 KB = 1024 bytes. Note that 1 kilobyte is 1024 not 1000 bytes because computers work in powers of 2.

templates.pattern: A file has a size of [KB] KB. Calculate the size of the file in megabytes (MB).
templates.explanation:
File size in MB = KB ÷ 1024
= [KB] ÷ 1024
= [RESULT] MB

1 MB = 1024 KB = 1,048,576 bytes. These conversions are essential for calculating storage requirements.

templates.pattern: A colour palette uses [N] bits per pixel. Calculate the maximum number of different colours that can be represented.
templates.explanation:
Number of colours = 2ⁿ
= 2^[N]
= [RESULT]

Each additional bit doubles the number of available colours. 8-bit colour gives 256 colours, 16-bit gives 65,536 and 24-bit gives over 16 million colours.

templates.pattern: A colour palette contains [N] different colours. Calculate the minimum number of bits needed to represent each colour.
templates.explanation:
Bits needed = log₂(number of colours)
= log₂([N])
= [RESULT] bits

This is the inverse of 2ⁿ. If you need 256 colours you need log₂(256) = 8 bits per pixel. Always round up if the answer is not a whole number.

templates.pattern: A bitmap image is [W] pixels wide and [H] pixels tall with a colour depth of [D] bits per pixel. Calculate the file size of the image in kilobytes (KB).
templates.explanation:
File size in KB = (W × H × D) ÷ 8 ÷ 1024
= ([W] × [H] × [D]) ÷ 8 ÷ 1024
= [W*H*D] ÷ 8 ÷ 1024
= [RESULT] KB

First calculate total bits, divide by 8 for bytes, then divide by 1024 for kilobytes.

templates.pattern: An audio recording has a sample rate of [SR] Hz and a bit depth of [BD] bits. Calculate the data generated per second in bits.
templates.explanation:
Data per second = sample rate × bit depth
= [SR] × [BD]
= [RESULT] bits/s

The sample rate determines how many times per second the audio is measured. The bit depth determines the precision of each measurement. Both affect file size and quality.

templates.pattern: A digital image is [W] pixels wide and [H] pixels tall. Calculate the total number of pixels in the image.
templates.explanation:
Total pixels = width × height
= [W] × [H]
= [RESULT] pixels

The total number of pixels determines the resolution of an image. More pixels means higher resolution and more detail but also larger file size.

templates.pattern: A storage device has a capacity of [MB] MB. Calculate the storage capacity in gigabytes (GB).
templates.explanation:
Storage in GB = MB ÷ 1024
= [MB] ÷ 1024
= [RESULT] GB

1 GB = 1024 MB. Modern storage devices are measured in gigabytes or terabytes. A 1 TB drive holds 1024 GB = 1,048,576 MB.
